How to choose an aircraft model as a gift

The best aircraft model gift is often the airplane with a story. Choose the right type, scale and display format before deciding how much to spend.

By Pilot Gift Guide · From the team behind ATC · How we choose

IN THIS GUIDEFind the airplane with personal meaningCheck what the model representsMeasure the destination, not just the modelChoose finished model or building projectThe gift shortlist

Find the airplane with personal meaning

Ask about the recipient’s first lesson, first solo, favorite airline or memorable airshow. A model connected to that story can be more meaningful than a large generic jet. Get the aircraft name and variant right. If you are unsure, a photograph is useful: the recipient or a knowledgeable friend may be able to identify it without you needing to learn every designation.

Check what the model represents

Two listings can name the same aircraft family while showing different versions, markings or finishes. Collectors may care about those distinctions. Check photographs from multiple angles, the stated material and whether a stand is included. If the listing describes a handcrafted item, find out whether small differences are expected. Personalization should only be ordered after the spelling and any registration details are confirmed.

Measure the destination, not just the model

A model needs room for its wings, stand and safe handling. Measure the shelf or desk where it might live and leave clearance around delicate parts. A long aircraft can look compact in a product photograph. LEGO’s Concorde, for example, needs a substantial display area once assembled. If the recipient lives in a small apartment, a smaller keepsake may be a more considerate choice.

Choose finished model or building project

A finished model suits someone who wants to display an aircraft immediately. A construction set suits someone who enjoys the process. Neither is automatically more thoughtful. If you want the gift to become a shared activity, ask whether the recipient would enjoy building together. Keep the option easy to decline; a gift should not arrive as an obligation to complete a project on your schedule.
